title: Sign Language Recognition and Translation for Low-Resource Languages: Challenges and Pathways Forward
abstract: arXiv:2605.12096v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Sign languages are natural, visual-gestural languages used by Deaf communities worldwide. Over 300 distinct sign languages remain severely low-resource due to limited documentation, sparse datasets, and insufficient computational tools. This systematic review synthesizes literature on sign language recognition and translation for under-resourced languages, using Azerbaijan Sign Language (AzSL) as a case study. Analysis of global initiatives extracts eight actionable lessons, including community co-design, dialectal diversity capture, and privacy-preserving pose-based representations. Turkic sign languages (Kazakh, Turkish, Azerbaijani) receive special attention, as linguistic proximity enables effective transfer learning. We propose three paradigm shifts: from architecture-centric to data-centric AI, from signer-independent to signer-adaptive systems, and from reference-based to task-specific evaluation metrics. translated_title: 面向低资源语言的手语识别与翻译：挑战与前进之路
translated_abstract: 手语是世界各地聋人群体使用的自然视觉-手势语言。由于文献记录有限、数据集稀疏以及计算工具不足，超过300种不同的手语仍处于严重的低资源状态。本系统性综述综合了关于低资源语言手语识别与翻译的相关文献，并以阿塞拜疆手语（AzSL）作为案例研究。通过对全球倡议的分析，提炼出八条可操作的经验教训，包括社区共同设计、方言多样性采集以及隐私保护的基于姿态的表示方法。突厥语系手语（哈萨克语、土耳其语、阿塞拜疆语）受到特别关注，因为语言上的相近性使得迁移学习能够有效开展。我们提出了三个范式转变：从以架构为中心的AI转向以数据为中心的AI，从手语使用者无关的系统转向手语使用者自适应的系统，以及从基于参考的评估指标转向面向特定任务的评估指标。最后给出了技术路线图。
tldr: 本综述以阿塞拜疆手语为案例，系统梳理了低资源手语识别与翻译面临的挑战，提炼出八条可操作经验，并提出以数据为中心的AI、手语使用者自适应系统和任务导向评估指标这三大范式转变。
en_tdlr: This systematic review uses Azerbaijan Sign Language as a case study to synthesize challenges in low-resource sign language recognition and translation, extracting eight actionable lessons and proposing three paradigm shifts: from architecture-centric to data-centric AI, from signer-independent to signer-adaptive systems, and from reference-based to task-specific evaluation metrics.
